newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel hits new low against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel hits new low against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed at a new low against the dollar on Tuesday as the U.S. currency continued rising on overseas markets, dealers said.

"The shekel continued to decline against the dollar as the dollar rose abroad. Overall, trading was very quiet today and the dollar moved in a narrow range of 3.3860 to 3.3890," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.

"The basket traded slightly under the lower edge of the trading band and the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market, buying dollars on a relatively low scale. I believe that the central bank purchased $50 million to $100 million," the dealer said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3890 shekels against 3.3810 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6656 shekels against 3.6651 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6848 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6982 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9772 shekels after 1.9856 on Monday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3880 shekels.
